title: Ancient Trees in Slovakia: Cities to Explore
meta_description: Slovakia's oldest tree isn't the famous one. An oak in Dubinné, hollow past dating, is reckoned at 800 years plus. 18 places mapped, 27 trees.
intro: Slovakia's most-told tree story belongs to Bojnice, where a linden behind the castle is tied by tradition to a visit from King Matthias Corvinus and put at over 700 years, no measurement behind the round number. The better-documented tree is a plainer oak in Dubinné, near Bardejov, hollow enough that the wood which would date it has rotted away, leaving a working estimate of at least 800 years and the country's own claim to its oldest oak. Most of the rest of the oldest trees here are lindens, which is not a coincidence: the lime has been Slovakia's national tree since the 13th century. Hronsek's stand in the yard of a UNESCO wooden church; Uzovská Panica keeps something rarer, a 250-year-old service tree that once marked a property line. Bratislava's own collection reads almost as an inventory of other continents: a Japanese pagoda tree on the Danube embankment, an Empress tree from China, a paper birch that belongs in Canada. 27 trees across 18 places now, and the plainest one, not the castle linden, is the oldest.
